title.value: Knowledge Sharing via Domain Adaptation in Customs Fraud Detection
title.justification: The paper's title 'Knowledge Sharing via Domain Adaptation in Customs Fraud Detection' directly reflects the main focus of the research, which is on using domain adaptation for knowledge sharing in customs fraud detection.
title.quote: Knowledge Sharing via Domain Adaptation in Customs Fraud Detection

extractions.description: The paper presents a system called DAS for enhancing customs fraud detection across countries by sharing knowledge through domain adaptation. DAS employs a memory bank platform to enable multi-national customs administrations to share and utilize transferable knowledge of trade frauds. The system enhances fraud detection at the national level by refining local models with shared prototypes, thereby addressing infrastructure limitations in participating countries and improving the detection of illicit trades.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is enhancing customs fraud detection through domain adaptation and knowledge sharing, which primarily impacts tax revenue and illicit trade detection rather than directly addressing climate or ecologically-related sustainable development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The detection process has traditionally used rule-based algorithms, which is gradually changing to machine learning algorithms (Mikuriya and Cantens 2021).

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on enhancing customs fraud detection through domain adaptation and does not directly address any particular aspect of climate or ecologically-related sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: In practice, DAS can be adopted among countries under bilateral and regional trade agreements to accelerate market opening and pursue higher levels of trade freedom.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category for climate or ecologically-related sustainable development within the paper's scope, as it is primarily concerned with the mechanics of fraud detection through shared knowledge.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a domain adaptation method to share transferable knowledge of frauds as prototypes while safeguarding the local trade information.

applications.justification: The application of the research is in customs fraud detection, as the paper proposes a system (DAS) for enhancing customs fraud detection through shared knowledge across international borders.
applications.quote: This research proposes a first-of-a-kind collaborative customs fraud detection system that enables information sharing across regional boundaries.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce a new category within climate or ecologically-related sustainable development but focuses instead on customs fraud detection.
new_primary_category.quote: The World Customs Organization (WCO) has been leading such data initiatives by assisting customs offices in 175 countries with their digital transformation process (Weerth 2009).

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no novel sub-category related to climate or ecologically-related sustainable development introduced in this paper, which remains focused on customs fraud detection through domain adaptation techniques.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We use techniques in domain adaptation and propose a new data prototyping method to extract transferable knowledge from import declarations.
